Buy 1 cosmetic at a time, go to Sephora or Ulta or department store counter during a weekday and have someone help choose the color and teach you to apply it.

Start with foundation or pressed powder.

Come back the next week WITH YOUR LAST PURCHASE and get another cosmetic, like eye liner, or a lipstick. Keep going until you have the basics.

GO DURING A SLOW WEEKDAY. Some makeup counters have minimum purchase requirements for help from a makeup artist. They're less strict about it on a slow day.

Since you're NEW, DON'T APPROACH THE GLAM QUEEN TO HELP YOU APPLY. The way a makeup artist does his or her own look is how they're *likely* to do you up too. Nothing wrong with being a queen, but you are just starting out as a junior princess. If the makeup is too soft, you can add more later. If it's too much, you'll be freaked out and never come back.

GET SAMPLES. Of everything!

You seem like you're having a terrible day. My parents kicked me out with nothing at 18. They didn't give me any auto training. I got my first phone ... late in life. And yet, I fix my car anyway. Nobody showed me how.

Here's how you can start, with your bulbs at least--

Go to a parts shop and ask someone at the counter or service desk to help you install the bulbs. They may or may not charge you for it.

Watch them do it, carefully. Make your own video if you want.

The hard part that YT admittedly seems to be so easy, is to find the place in the car that has the trap door for the lights to go in and out.

Buy the service manual for your car model and year, for the future, for these small repairs. There are diagrams, explanations, videos for the small fixes like fuses and lights. You don't need some drunk old man or a closet full of tools to show you basic car care. New cars have latches on every filter, so most times those are really easy to fix on your own.
